findings.title: Task 11 makes `detect()` throw, which breaks existing mocked detector tests and widens failures to every `detect()` caller
findings.description:
Task 11 has `detect()` throw when `checkSyncStatus()` returns `'error'`.
- The existing submodule tests (`GuideDetector.test.ts:68-90`, `92-114`, `205-226`) mock `gitExec` to throw for anything except `describe`. `checkSyncStatus()` would then return `'error'`, and `detect()` would throw in tests that currently pass.
- Task 4 only renames `manual` → `tarball`. Task 12 only adds tests. No task updates these mocks.
- `checkSyncStatus()` (`GuideDetector.ts:159`) discards the underlying git error. The thrown error would lose the "not a repo / git missing" detail D1/D7 wants surfaced.
- `detect()` is also called by `GuideManager.install/update/uninstall/syncWorktrees/status` (`GuideManager.ts:29,39,60,91,147`), `setup-ide.ts:106`, and the `cf version --json` path. Any git hiccup now fails `cf guides uninstall` and `cf guides update`. This is not the read-only status the design intends for `cf guides info`.
- `GuideInfo.checkout` is a required field. The typed `GuideInfo` literals in `GuideManager.test.ts:72,83,292,591` need the field. Task 10 only says typecheck passes "once Task 11 populates the field".

Fix: do the throw only in `ensureCheckout()`, or have `detect()` record `'error'` and let callers decide. Add an explicit step to update the existing mocked detector tests and `GuideInfo` fixtures.

findings.title: Tasks 22/23: the MCP `notices[]` shape can't be implemented against the current tool results
findings.description:
`context_build` returns `textResult(contextString)` (`contextTools.ts:165`), and `prompt_get` returns `textResult(header + content)` (`:299`). Both are `{content:[{type:'text',text}]}`, with no object to hang a `notices` array on.
- Only `prompt_list` (`jsonResult`) has a JSON payload.
- Task 23 asserts "no `notices` key (or empty array — pick one)" on `context_build`, which has no keys.
- `generateContext()` returns a `string`, and `resolvePromptFileForTools()` returns a path `string`. Neither can carry notices without a signature change that no task mentions.
- Task 22 places the call "before `createContextPipeline` (~line 57)". That is inside `generateContext()`, which `template_preview` also calls. `template_preview` and `prompt_list`/`prompt_get` are annotated `readOnlyHint: true`, and `template_preview`'s description says "without … triggering any side effects". They would now perform a network fetch, and `template_preview` would have no channel for the notice.

Fix: specify the concrete shape, for example an extra `{type:'text'}` content block for text tools and a `notices` field for JSON tools. Decide whether `template_preview` is wired or explicitly excluded (this affects the D3 "cover every hit" rule). Reconcile the `readOnlyHint` annotations.

findings.title: Tasks 20/21/23/26/27 break existing CLI and MCP tests that mock core and `guides.js`, and none of them schedule the mock updates
findings.description:
Several existing suites mock their dependencies wholesale:
- `build.test.ts:9-20` mocks `@context-forge/core/node` with only `FileProjectStore`, `createContextPipeline` and `ConfigManager`. `prompt.test.ts:10` and `setup-ide.test.ts:28` mock the same module.
- `init.test.ts:42` mocks `../../src/commands/guides.js` with only `guidesInstallAction` and `registerGuidesCommand`. It mocks `@context-forge/core/node` with only `FileProjectStore`.
- `contextTools.test.ts:20` and `guideTools.test.ts:18` also mock core.

Consequences:
- `ensureGuideReady()` imports `GuideManager` from core, so every existing build/prompt/setup-ide test breaks once Task 20 lands.
- `init.ts` importing `strategyHelpText` from `guides.js`, or `normalizeGuideMethod` from core, hits an undefined mock export. That breaks all existing `init.test.ts` tests at `registerInitCommand` time.
- Task 21 wants a real-git `cloned()` fixture "in `build.test.ts`" with a "registered project". That file mocks the store, core and pipeline, so a real-git fixture cannot work there.
- Task 23 uses the `cloned()` fixture for `guide_status`. `guideTools.test.ts` mocks `GuideManager.status`, so "does not initialize" is untestable there.
- The Task 9 fixture lives under `packages/core/tests/guides/helpers/`. CLI and MCP tests cannot import it across package boundaries without rootDir/tsconfig changes.

Fix: add explicit mock-update steps. Mock `guideReady.js` in the existing command tests. Test `ensureGuideReady` in its own test file with a mocked `GuideManager`. Keep real-git end-to-end coverage in core, or in a clearly separate integration test with its own fixture access.

findings.title: Tasks 13/14 rest on a wrong claim about `NETWORK_ERROR_PATTERNS`
findings.description:
Task 13 says "the `/timed out/i` pattern already matches". The slice D10 says the same. The patterns are `/could not resolve host/i`, `/could not connect to/i`, `/connection timed out/i`, `/network is unreachable/i`, `/ssl certificate problem/i`, `/failed to connect/i`, `/enotfound/i`, `/econnrefused/i`, `/etimedout/i`. A message like "git … timed out after 60 seconds" matches none of them.
- Following Task 13 literally, the remediation text is not appended, and Task 14's assertion for `GUIDE_OFFLINE_REMEDIATION` fails.
- Node's `execFile` timeout error is "Command failed: …" with `killed: true` and `signal: 'SIGTERM'`, and the callback receives it without any "timed out" text.

Fix: say that the timeout branch detects `error.killed`, builds the message itself, and either includes "connection timed out" or appends the remediation explicitly. Also note that SIGTERM to `git submodule update` may not stop its child `git-remote-https`.

findings.title: Task 9 misdescribes `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` and omits the local-protocol restriction on submodule fixtures
findings.description:
The task file and slice both say existing guide tests create temp repos, and Task 9 points at `SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts` for a "real-git temp-repo pattern".
- That file mocks `fs` and `gitExec` entirely (lines 5-14), and so does `GuideDetector.test.ts`. No guide test uses real git. The "extend it rather than duplicating" step has nothing to extend.
- Modern git (2.38.1+) rejects `git submodule add/update` from a local-path URL unless `protocol.file.allow=always` is set. Nothing under `packages/` mentions `protocol.file.allow`.
- The fixture's `initialized()` and `cloned()` steps, and `SubmoduleStrategy.init()` itself running through `gitExec`, will fail with "transport 'file' not allowed". `gitExec` spreads `process.env`, so the helper must set `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`/`KEY_0`/`VALUE_0` (or equivalent).

Fix: correct the claim and add the protocol-allow requirement and env mechanism to Task 9. Task 9's size-3 estimate is reasonable once this is stated.

findings.title: Task 4's commit lands with CLI and MCP broken
findings.description:
After Tasks 3-4 the `GuideMethod` rename is committed, but the boundary packages are not updated until Task 7.
- The MCP zod enum (`guideTools.ts:101`) still emits `'manual'`, which no longer type-checks against `GuideMethod`.
- The CLI cast `opts.strategy as GuideMethod` (`guides.ts:125`) lets `--strategy manual` through. `getStrategy('manual')` in `GuideManager.ts:214-223` then returns `undefined`, and `install()` throws a TypeError.
- Task 4's criterion is only the core test suite. `pnpm -r build` would fail at this commit.

Fix: move the Task 4 commit marker to after Task 8, or fold Task 7 into the first working point. Task 32's walkthrough also has to use whichever commit is final.

findings.title: Task 3's success grep misses the double-quoted `"manual"` strings and a site the design doesn't list
findings.description:
The criterion `grep -rn "'manual'"` uses single quotes. The user-facing error text uses double quotes:
- `CloneStrategy.ts:34`: `use the "manual" strategy`
- `SubmoduleStrategy.ts:39`: `use the "manual" strategy`
- `SubmoduleStrategy.ts:45`: `Use --strategy clone or --strategy manual`

These point users at the deprecated name and pass the grep. `SubmoduleStrategy.ts:45` is not in the design's "Rename sweep" list. Comments at `TarballStrategy.ts:1` and `GuideManager.ts:135` also say manual. Fix: grep for `manual` case-insensitively and enumerate these locations.

findings.title: Task 5: optional `ConfigManager`, undecided return shape, and an uncovered MCP config-alias path
findings.description:
- `GuideManager`'s `configManager` is optional (`GuideManager.ts:15,19`). Task 5 says "no fallback branch is needed" and returns `normalizeGuideMethod(configValue)` from `ConfigManager.get()`. With no `ConfigManager` there is no value, so the default must come from `CONFIG_KEYS['guide.git_strategy'].default`. The task never says to read it there, and a junior would reintroduce a literal.
- The return shape for surfacing a deprecated alias is left as "choose one", yet Tasks 6(b) and 7 depend on it. `install()` returns `InstallResult` and is JSON-serialized by the MCP tool. Whether the alias flag rides on the result is unspecified.
- D5 requires an MCP notice for the config-path alias too. Task 7 adds an MCP notice only for the `strategy` parameter, so a shared config with `manual` installed through `guide_install` has no notice.
- The CLI config-path warning has no test. Task 8 covers only `--strategy manual`. The slice criterion "shared config `manual` installs as tarball with the same warning" is tested only at core level.

findings.title: Task 26: `--strategy bogus` can't "fail before any install" as the task is structured
findings.description:
Task 27 expects `cf init --strategy bogus` to fail with the valid-values message before any install. In `init.ts`, the project is registered at line 104 (`store.create`), and the install runs inside a `try/catch` at lines 117-127. That catch prints `Guides install failed: …` and continues to IDE setup, exiting 0. Calling `normalizeGuideMethod` inside the try would be swallowed. Validating after line 104 would leave a registered project behind.

Fix: say to validate the option at the top of the action, before any store writes and outside the catch. Also state what `--lite --strategy x` does. Alias normalization and warning logic is also spelled twice (Task 7 and Task 26). Specify one shared helper rather than duplicating it.

findings.title: Task 20 places the `prompt get` wiring after the first guide read, and `setup-ide` has no `operationPath`
findings.description:
Task 20 says to wire `prompt.ts` at "~lines 60 and 116".
- In `prompt get`, line 114 calls `resolvePhaseInput(phase, opPath)`. For `P1`-style input this reads the prompt file via `getPhaseShorthands` (`phaseShorthand.ts:22-23`), so an `ensureGuideReady` placed before line 116 runs after the first read. The shorthand path would hit ENOENT on an empty tree. The call must go before line 114.
- `phaseShorthand.ts:22` is a guide read the task's own grep would surface, but it is not listed. The cached `cachedShorthands` could also hold results from an empty tree.
- `setupIdeAction(projectPath, target, opts)` (`setup-ide.ts:93`) takes no `operationPath`, and `init.ts:151` calls it with just `cwd`. Task 19's `ensureGuideReady(projectPath, operationPath)` has no value to pass there. Either the signature changes (which affects `init.test.ts` mocks) or `projectPath` is used. The task doesn't say.
- Task 20 asks to "list covered call sites in the commit body", but Task 20 has no commit marker. The commit is at Task 21.

findings.title: `ensureCheckout()` via `detect()` adds an unbounded `git ls-remote` to every read command
findings.description:
`detect()` always calls `fetchLatestVersion()` (`git ls-remote --tags`, no timeout) when the guide exists (`GuideDetector.ts:89`). Task 17 uses `detector.detect()` as the primary read.
- Every `cf build`, `cf prompt` and MCP `context_build`/`prompt_*` now makes a network call it didn't make before. Behind the blackholed-proxy case that D10/F004 identifies, each read command hangs for the OS TCP timeout. D10 bounds only the init fetch.
- `detectVersion()` on an uninitialized gitlink runs `git describe` in the empty guide dir, which resolves against the host repo. The version reported for `not_initialized` is the host repo's tag or null.

Fix: have `ensureCheckout()` use a lightweight path (method plus `checkSyncStatus`) that skips `fetchLatestVersion`. If `detect()` stays, state the cost and cover it.

findings.title: Task 15: `init()` signature contradicts its own use, and existing `sync()` tests pin call arguments
findings.description:
Task 15 defines `init(operationPath)` and says it runs with `{ timeoutMs: GUIDE_INIT_TIMEOUT_MS }`. It then says `sync()` must call it "without the timeout: pass the timeout as an `init()` option". Whether the default is bounded or unbounded is never stated, and `ensureCheckout()` (Task 17) needs the bounded form.
- The existing `sync()` test asserts `gitExec` was called with exactly `['submodule','update','--init',GUIDE_RELATIVE_PATH], worktreePath` (`SubmoduleStrategy.test.ts:220-223`). A third argument, even `undefined`, risks failing that assertion.
- `sync()` also gains an extra `rev-parse` call.

Fix: give one signature (for example `init(path, opts?: { timeoutMs?: number })`, with `ensureCheckout` passing the constant). State that the existing sync assertions are expected to hold. `sync()` can also skip the `rev-parse`.

findings.title: Task 32: the walkthrough clone isn't a registered project, so the steps don't exercise the clone
findings.description:
Walkthrough step 1 clones `/tmp/g925` to `/tmp/g925-clone` and runs `cf guides info` and `cf build` there. Project resolution is by cwd against registered `projectPath` (`packages/cli/src/utils/project.ts:42-68,144-149`). The clone isn't registered, so commands resolve to a different project or none. Task 32 runs the steps verbatim.

Fix: add a `cf init --lite` (or project registration) in the clone, or use `--project` with a path-registered entry, so the auto-init is tested. Also say the walkthrough registers throwaway projects in the real user store, and make the cleanup (step 5) run even if an earlier step fails.

findings.title: Commit markers use the wrong form and are dense
findings.description: Markers are embedded as `Commit: …` inside the Success-criteria checkbox bullets, not as plain `**Commit**:` lines. They appear after 13 of 32 tasks (4, 6, 8, 12, 14, 16, 18, 21, 23, 24, 27, 29, 31). Most sit at tested points, apart from Task 4 (see above). Task 14's tiny `gitExec` commit and Task 16's refactor commit could be one commit with Tasks 13-18.

findings.title: Proportionality: some tasks can merge
findings.description:
- Tasks 28-29 (a one-line constant plus printing it and its test) edit the same `showStatus()` and `guides.test.ts` as Task 24. Fold them into Task 24.
- Task 2 is separate from Task 1 only by tests. Task 10 is too granular on its own (types plus one retype).
- The README task's success check `grep "overwritten on" README.md` depends on the D9 sentence being present, which is fine.

Part 4 tests (Task 27) also duplicate the help check across `help.test.ts` and `guides.test.ts` when one assertion suffices. No load-test or CI task is needed, because the slice restates no NFR.

findings.title: Task 32 and existing-code claims otherwise hold
findings.description: Verified accurate: the `GuideManager.ts` catches (lines 177, 192), the `'submodule'` literal at line 196, `GuideDetector.checkSyncStatus` parsing `+`/`-`, `GuideMethod` at `types.ts:4`, `ConfigKeys.ts:34`, the `guideTools.ts:47,93,101` locations, `guides.ts:119,125`, `build.ts:78`, `contextTools.ts:57,98`, and `setup-ide.ts:106`. After a killed or failed auto-init, git's clone cleanup leaves the gitlink uninitialized, so the next read retries. `cf guides info` remains the read-only path. Note that `resolveSource()` losing its catch means a malformed config now also fails `cf guides info`, `cf build` and `guide_status`. That is consistent with D7 but worth a line in the CHANGELOG.
